title: Acute respiratory illness and return to sport: a systematic review and meta-analysis by a subgroup of the IOC consensus on 'acute respiratory illness in the athlete'
authors: Snyders C, Pyne DB, Sewry N, Hull JH, Kaulback K, Schwellnus M
population: Athletes and military recruits aged 15-65 with symptoms or diagnosis of acute respiratory illness (54 studies)
findings: 767 articles identified; 54 included (n = 31,065 athletes); PubMed, EBSCOhost and Web of Science searched January 1990 to July 2020.
Only 4 studies reported days until return to sport (range 0 to 8.5 days).
Frequency of time loss >1 day after acute respiratory illness was 20.4% (95% CI 15.3% to 25.4%); in 80% of illnesses no days were lost from training/competition.
Mean symptom duration was 7.1 days (95% CI 6.2 to 8.0), similar across pathological and anatomical classifications and diagnostic methods.
Authors state current data are limited and standardised definitions are needed to inform return to sport.
limitations: Return-to-sport days from only 4 studies; no symptom-severity stratification or graded return protocol in the abstract; mixed athlete and military populations.
implications: Plan for about a week of symptoms when a respiratory illness is logged (mean 7.1 days); offer a short ease/skip option rather than a long plan reset.
A graded re-introduction (easy runs first, intensity only after symptom-free days) is an engine safety convention, not a finding of this paper, and must be labelled as such.
Do not let HRV or resting HR alone declare illness; use a logged symptom flag to suspend intensity.

verification.notes: Crossref confirms title, BJSM, first author Snyders, online 17 Nov 2021 (print 2022). Numbers verified in Europe PMC abstract (PMID 34789459).
